message:
Hi. I'm off to Lisbon next week for a three-day work trip, my first time in Portugal, and I want to travel carry-on only this time, after the airline lost my case in the spring.

Could you suggest three things to do in Lisbon on a free evening? And how do I say "thank you" in Portuguese? Is it different depending on who's saying it? And is tipping expected in restaurants there, or is that more of an American thing?

My wheeled bag measures 56 × 36 × 23 cm including the wheels and handle, and packed it weighs 9 kg. Will it meet the carry-on limit?

Also, recommend a packing approach: rolling or folding for work shirts? I need a short out-of-office message that's professional but not stiff, since most of my contacts are clients rather than colleagues. And what's a good colour for a luggage tag so it's easy to spot? I'm flying back on the Friday evening, straight after a full day of meetings, so anything that makes the return journey less stressful is welcome.

Thanks a lot.
response:
Here's everything, in roughly the order you'll need it.

## Will your bag meet the carry-on limit?

**It depends entirely on the airline and fare, so check before you go.** Your bag is 56 × 36 × 23 cm and 9 kg. Many airlines on European routes use a 55 × 40 × 20 cm limit, which your bag exceeds by 1 cm in length and 3 cm in depth. Limits on some common carriers, as I understand them:

| Airline | Cabin bag limit | Your bag (56 × 36 × 23 cm, 9 kg) |
|---|---|---|
| British Airways | 56 × 45 × 25 cm, up to 23 kg | ✓ fits |
| easyJet (large cabin bag, paid add-on) | 56 × 45 × 25 cm, up to 15 kg | ✓ fits |
| TAP Air Portugal | 55 × 40 × 20 cm, 8 kg | ✗ too long, too deep and too heavy |
| Ryanair (Priority) | 55 × 40 × 20 cm, 10 kg | ✗ too long and too deep |
| Lufthansa | 55 × 40 × 23 cm, 8 kg | ✗ 1 cm too long, 1 kg over |

Airlines change these limits, and the allowance can depend on your fare type, so confirm on your booking page. If your airline uses 55 × 40 × 20 cm, a soft bag or a smaller case is the safer choice. An overlong bag can be sent to the hold at the gate, which is exactly what you're trying to avoid.

## Three things to do on a free evening

1. **Watch the sunset from a miradouro (viewpoint).** Senhora do Monte and Santa Luzia have some of the best views across the city and river.
2. **Wander Alfama and hear fado.** Alfama is the old quarter, a maze of lanes, and in the evening many small restaurants there host fado, Portugal's traditional song. Book ahead or arrive early.
3. **Dinner and drinks in Bairro Alto or Príncipe Real.** Bairro Alto gets lively after dark, and Príncipe Real nearby is calmer and good for dinner.

Try at least one *pastel de nata*, the custard tart, while you're there.

## Saying "thank you"

It depends on **who is speaking**, not who you're thanking:
- **Obrigado** (roughly *oh-bree-GAH-doo*) if you're a man
- **Obrigada** (roughly *oh-bree-GAH-dah*) if you're a woman

## Tipping

Tipping isn't expected the way it is in the US. Locals often round up or leave small change. In restaurants, about **5–10% for good service** is appreciated but not obligatory. Service charges are rarely added to the bill.

## Rolling or folding work shirts?

**Fold, don't roll.** Rolling suits casual clothes, but it tends to crease dress shirts along their length. Button each shirt, fold it around a stiff piece of card or a folding board, and lay the shirts flat on top of the bag. When you arrive, hang them in the bathroom while you shower, and the steam will ease out minor creases. Most business hotels can also provide an iron.

## Out-of-office message

> Thank you for your email. I'm travelling for work from [date] to [date] with limited access to email, so my replies may be slower than usual. I'll respond as soon as I can on my return. For anything urgent, please contact [Name] at [email/phone].
>
> Best regards,
> [Your name]

## Luggage tag colour

Choose **a bright colour that's rare on luggage**, such as neon orange, lime green or hot pink. Most bags are black, grey or navy, so a vivid tag stands out immediately. It's worth having even on carry-on, in case the bag is taken at the gate.

## Making the Friday return easier

- **Pack on Friday morning**, before your meetings, and leave your bag at hotel reception or bring it with you. Don't plan to go back to the hotel.
- **Check in online** and keep your boarding pass on your phone.
- **Allow plenty of time.** Lisbon airport is close to the city, about 20–30 minutes by taxi or metro, but it's often busy, and security queues can be long on Friday evenings. Arriving about two hours before departure is sensible.
- **Pack for security.** Keep liquids under 100 ml in a clear bag and your laptop easy to reach.
- **Keep a change of clothes or a fresh shirt** in your bag if you want to freshen up after meetings.

Have a great trip.
